entities.name: Bat
entities.primary_domains: sky; cattle; cosmic protection; nome tutelary
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Archaic bovine sky-goddess of the 7th Upper Egyptian nome, depicted as the inward-curling-horned cow head atop the Narmer Palette (Dyn. 0/1) and later absorbed by Hathor.

entities.name: Mehit
entities.primary_domains: lioness ferocity; nome tutelary; consort of Anhur
entities.source: Wilkinson, Early Dynastic Egypt; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Lioness goddess of This/Thinis whose recumbent-lioness emblem is attested already in the Early Dynastic period; consort of Anhur (Onuris).

entities.name: Sed
entities.primary_domains: royal jubilee (heb-sed); protection of the king; canine power
entities.source: Wilkinson, Early Dynastic Egypt; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Archaic jackal/wolf-form deity for whom the royal Sed (jubilee) festival is named, attested from the 1st Dynasty and associated with Wepwawet.

entities.name: Dunanwi
entities.primary_domains: falcon kingship; nome tutelary; eastern sky
entities.note: Falcon tutelary of the 18th Upper Egyptian nome, named in the Pyramid Texts and later largely assimilated to Horus.

entities.name: Khenty-irty
entities.primary_domains: sight and blindness (sun and moon eyes); guardianship; kingship
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Falcon god of Letopolis appearing as Khenty-irty ('Foremost of the Two Eyes')/Khenty-khety; attested from the Old Kingdom and linked to the waxing and waning of celestial light.

entities.name: Sepa
entities.primary_domains: protection against venomous bites; soil fertility; funerary protection
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Centipede god of Heliopolis invoked against venomous creatures; attested from the Old Kingdom and later identified with Osiris.

entities.name: Hededet
entities.primary_domains: scorpion protection; healing of stings; maternal protection
entities.note: Scorpion goddess named in the Pyramid Texts, a protective scorpion power later assimilated to Isis.

entities.name: Khenti-kheti
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Local god of Athribis (10th Lower Egyptian nome), originally crocodile-form and later falcon-form (Horus-Khenti-kheti), attested from the Old Kingdom.

entities.name: Souls of Pe
entities.primary_domains: deceased predynastic kings of Buto; royal ancestors; jubilation for the king
entities.source: Pyramid Texts; Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses
entities.note: Falcon-headed ancestral spirits of the predynastic rulers of Pe (Buto) in the Delta, invoked acclaiming the king in the Pyramid Texts.

entities.name: Souls of Nekhen
entities.primary_domains: deceased predynastic kings of Hierakonpolis; royal ancestors; jubilation for the king
entities.source: Pyramid Texts; Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses
entities.note: Jackal-headed ancestral spirits of the predynastic rulers of Nekhen (Hierakonpolis) in Upper Egypt, paired with the Souls of Pe in the Pyramid Texts.

entities.name: Iabet
entities.source: Hart, Routledge Dictionary; Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses
entities.note: Goddess personifying the East (Iabtet), counterpart of Imentet the West, attested from the Old Kingdom and associated with the rising sun.

entities.name: Imentet
entities.primary_domains: the western direction; the necropolis; welcoming the dead
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Goddess of the West and the realm of the dead, wearing the West (imnt) emblem on her head, attested from the Old Kingdom and closely linked to Hathor.

entities.name: Nebethetepet
entities.primary_domains: creation (hand of Atum); Heliopolitan generative power; satisfaction
entities.source: Hart, Routledge Dictionary; Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses
entities.note: Heliopolitan goddess ('Mistress of the Offering/Contentment') personifying the creative hand of Atum, associated with Iusaaset and Hathor from the Old Kingdom onward.

entities.name: Iunit
entities.primary_domains: nome tutelary; consort of Montu; the town of Iuni/Hermonthis
entities.source: Hart, Routledge Dictionary; Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses
entities.note: Local goddess of Hermonthis/Armant (Iuni), a consort of Montu in the Theban region, attested from the Middle Kingdom.

entities.name: Henkhisesui
entities.primary_domains: the east wind; weather; cardinal-wind personification
entities.note: Personification of the east wind, one of the cardinal-wind deities, attested as a ram- or scarab-form figure and linked to Anhur.

entities.name: Seret
entities.note: Lioness goddess associated with a Delta locality, one of the archaic feline tutelaries grouped with Bastet and Sekhmet.

entities.name: Aha
entities.primary_domains: household and birth protection; warding evil; combat with serpents
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: Aha ('the Fighter'), a leonine-dwarf apotropaic deity depicted strangling serpents on Middle Kingdom 'magic wands', an early antecedent of Bes.

entities.name: Sefkhet-Abwy
entities.primary_domains: writing; building measurement; royal records; counting years of reign
entities.source: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses; Hart, Routledge Dictionary
entities.note: 'She of the Seven Horns', a form/aspect of the writing goddess associated with the foundation-ceremony 'stretching of the cord', attested from the Old Kingdom alongside Seshat.

relationships.rationale: The archaic cow-goddess Bat was progressively absorbed into Hathor, who took over her sistrum/cow iconography by the Middle Kingdom.
Bat's emblem flanks the king beside Horus imagery on the Narmer Palette, expressing her role in legitimating Horus-kingship.
Mehit is the consort of Anhur (Onuris) at This, mythologized as the distant lioness brought back from Nubia.
As a lioness goddess Mehit embodies ferocity and martial protective power.
The archaic canine deity Sed was identified with the jackal/wolf opener-of-the-ways Wepwawet in royal jubilee contexts.
Sed presides over the royal jubilee (heb-sed) renewing the reign of the living Horus-king.
The falcon nome-god Dunanwi was assimilated to Horus, whose falcon form subsumed local falcon tutelaries.
Khenty-irty of Letopolis was identified with Horus as Horus-Khenty-irty, sharing the falcon and the solar/lunar eyes.
His names 'Khenty-irty' (with eyes) and 'Khenty-en-irty' (without eyes) express the waxing and waning of celestial light.
The centipede god Sepa was invoked to protect against venomous bites and stings.
Sepa was associated and merged with Osiris (Osiris-Sepa) at Heliopolis.
The scorpion goddess Hededet was assimilated to Isis, herself protectress against scorpions (Isis-Hededet).
Hededet personifies the scorpion's sting and its apotropaic, healing reversal.
The Athribite god Khenti-kheti, originally crocodile-form, became falcon-form as Horus-Khenti-kheti.
Khenti-kheti served as the protective tutelary of Athribis (10th Lower Egyptian nome).
The Souls of Pe (Lower Egypt) and Souls of Nekhen (Upper Egypt) are a fixed pair of royal-ancestor collectives in the Pyramid Texts.
The Souls of Pe acclaim and uphold the living Horus-king as predynastic royal ancestors of the Delta.
The Souls of Nekhen (Hierakonpolis, cult home of Horus) acclaim the king as Upper Egyptian royal ancestors.
Iabet (East) and Imentet (West) form a directional pair personifying the two horizons.
As personification of the East, Iabet is the place of sunrise and the rising sun.
Imentet, goddess of the West and the necropolis, was closely identified with Hathor as Lady of the West.
Imentet personifies the West as the realm of the dead and welcomes the deceased into the necropolis.
Nebethetepet personifies the creative hand of Atum, the female generative principle of his self-creation at Heliopolis.
Nebethetepet and Iusaaset are closely associated Heliopolitan goddesses both embodying Atum's creative agency.
Iunit is a consort goddess of Montu in the Theban/Hermonthis region.
Henkhisesui personifies the east wind among the cardinal-wind deities.
The east-wind deity is linked to Anhur in cardinal-wind iconography.
Seret is one of the archaic feline tutelaries grouped with the leonine goddesses Bastet and Sekhmet.
As a lioness nome goddess Seret embodies fierce protective power.
The Middle Kingdom leonine-dwarf protector Aha is the direct iconographic antecedent of Bes, absorbed into the Bes-image.
Aha ('the Fighter') is an apotropaic guardian of household, mother, and child, shown strangling serpents on magic wands.
Aha's serpent-strangling iconography casts him as a combatant of chaos-serpents akin to the Apophis-enemy.
Sefkhet-Abwy ('She of the Seven Horns') is a form/aspect of the writing-and-measurement goddess Seshat.
She governs writing, measurement, and the foundation-ceremony 'stretching of the cord' for temple building.
